props.title: It's a Free World...

sections.content: Ken Loach's **It's a Free World...** (2007) delivers a searing critique of labor exploitation in modern Britain. The film follows Angie, a recruitment agent who starts her own agency hiring migrant workers, gradually compromising her ethics for profit. Like Loach's **Riff-Raff** (1991) and **Bread and Roses** (2000), it exposes the harsh realities faced by vulnerable workers while examining how capitalism can corrupt ordinary people.

sections.content: The film connects thematically to other European works examining labor exploitation and immigration like **Welcome** (2009) and **Le Havre** (2011). These films share Loach's documentary-style realism and social consciousness, though his distinctly British perspective on class struggle sets **It's a Free World...** apart.

The performance by Kierston Wareing as Angie brings complexity to what could have been a simplistic morality tale. Like similar character studies in **Fish Tank** (2009) and **The Selfish Giant** (2013), the film shows how economic pressures can push working-class individuals toward ethical compromises. sections.content: Loach's film fits within the tradition of British social realist cinema that includes **This Is England** (2006) and **Sweet Sixteen** (2002). These films share an unflinching look at working-class life and social issues, using non-professional actors and location shooting to achieve authenticity.
